groups.text: It is currently 23 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

PyTorch developers have released a patch to resolve a specific indexing error within the forward automatic differentiation diagnostic path. This fix addresses a flaw where the fast-mode diagnostic path could select the wrong tensor or trigger an index error instead of a proper gradcheck error. The problem occurred when non-differentiable inputs or integer outputs appeared early in the sequence, causing the slow-mode error reporter to reuse incorrect indices. To solve this, the patch maps the fast-mode input index back to the original input tuple and recomputes the selected output within the correct indexing domain. This technical update does not break backward compatibility and was verified through a series of successful tests on CPU. The developers noted that they used ChatGPT to assist in drafting the technical summary and test notes for this release, though the fix itself targets the diagnostic path rather than normal gradcheck computation.

The human cost of the war in Ukraine continues to climb. The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost approximately 1,486,600 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,400 casualties suffered by Russian forces over the past day alone. The material losses are equally steep, with records showing the loss of 12,311 tanks and 25,248 armored combat vehicles. Russia has also lost 48,833 artillery systems, 1,594 air defense systems, and 440 aircraft. While Ukraine maintains operational secrecy regarding its own losses, a January report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated Ukrainian casualties between 500,000 and 600,000 through December 2025. That same think-tank suggests Russian casualties significantly surpass those of Ukraine, placing the ratio roughly between two to one or two and a half to one.

The death toll from flash floods in the Himalayas has risen to 750 people across Nepal and Tibet. In Nepal, disaster management officials have recovered 734 bodies, while Chinese authorities report 16 deaths in the southwest of the Tibet region. Search efforts continue for roughly 3,000 missing people, including 589 foreigners in Nepal. Many victims were swept kilometers downstream, with most bodies found in the Chitwan district near the Indian border. International aid from India and China has arrived as officials warn residents in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading of further potential flooding from the Bhotekoshi River. Meanwhile, in Switzerland, police are investigating a shooting at a techno rave in the city of Aarau. The Aargau cantonal police report at least one person dead and five others injured, some seriously, after shots were fired around 3 a.m. at a horse racing track in Schachen.

EU Commission President von der Leyen wants to significantly increase the EU budget, suggesting a total of nearly two trillion euros. However, Chancellor Merz and other EU heads of government are pushing for a smaller budget for the years 2028 through 2034. This tension stems from the fact that major contributors, led by Germany, face tight financial constraints and must implement their own austerity measures. While von der Leyen argues for more funding to address defense, migration, and competitiveness, the paying member states question why the EU should be an exception to current spending cuts. In a different sphere of risk, enterprises are scrambling to secure their operations as AI integrates into the workplace at breakneck speed. Organizations now face new insider threat models created by agentic AI and must establish governance guardrails to balance the power of these tools with essential security requirements.

Machine learning models now have an insatiable appetite for memory capacity, driving new hardware solutions to keep pace. To address this, XCENA and Samsung developed the MX1, a CXL memory expansion device fabricated using Samsung’s 4nm process. The MX1 can host up to two terabytes of DDR5 memory and features onboard compute powered by 3,072 RISC-V cores. While these hardware leaps expand capability, they exist alongside growing security vulnerabilities in the cloud. Many enterprises are currently struggling to identify and manage risks associated with their cloud applications and services. This gap is particularly acute as agentic AI introduces new insider threat models for organizations. Consequently, industry focus has shifted toward securing multi-cloud environments, as nearly every organization faced a critical security incident last year, yet most lacked the necessary tools to contain them.

In Iran, the regime continues to use intimidation and violence against female artists who perform in public. Recent convictions highlight these restrictions, with singer Hiva Seyfizadeh sentenced to four years in prison and Parastoo Ahmadi sentenced to 74 lashes. These penalties underscore a legal environment where women are forbidden from performing on stage before mixed audiences. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, the Lviv region is allocating two million hryvnias from its budget to purchase books directly from publishing warehouses. This move is intended to save printed editions and protect them from enemy destruction. In technical news, developers of llama.cpp have released a fix to prevent system crashes during context shifts of unquantized K cache. The update ensures the Hadamard matrix is copied to the k_rot tensor only when a buffer is assigned, stabilizing memory performance for users running local AI models across various operating systems.

Icelanders are leaning toward rejecting a return to European Union membership talks. Partial results from five of six constituencies show that 52.5 percent of voters oppose the government's proposal, while 47.5 percent support it. The current left-leaning government moved this referendum forward because of rising geopolitical tensions surrounding Greenland and Russia's war in Ukraine. While Iceland is already a member of the Schengen zone and the European Economic Area, the country has spent nearly two decades debating full accession. Talks were originally suspended thirteen years ago by a previous euroskeptic government. Some 270,000 citizens were eligible to vote in this referendum, though election officials warned that a more reliable final result might not be available until midday Sunday.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with rain chances up to 25 percent and temperatures between 24 and 27 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has Stefan Heinrichs' birthday today and a call with Jens at three in the afternoon.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
